currentQAWholeRecord.aiNotes: Actual independent image review: curricula/DE/Gymnasium/quality/goal-visualization-review/wirtschaft-e2-twenty-image-author-20261008-v1/independent-review/5b5ed3cb-7c2c-5b0f-a515-c967d8d23644/independent-image-review.receipt.json (sha256:b2cac4d5c570c8080f94fc5777e024112dd426b8d6c6b744a5a70895fda54067). One shopper compares two backpacks and thinks about budget, practical use and peers. Multiple influence types are distinguished without prescribing an allegedly rational choice or asserting a false price advantage. 360 px makes both alternatives, consumer reflection and the three large thought icons identifiable. 680 px shows both bags and utility/budget/social cues; no small print required. Store monitor faces the salesperson; learner-facing bags and symbolic thought bubbles have no directional text.

input.keepFormatDecision: Retain the good existing PNG and its close-native16:9 composition, already suitable for360 and680px. No format/provider/ratio normalization or regeneration is warranted.

findings.actualNativeImageObservation: A thoughtful shopper compares two large unbranded backpacks at a store counter. Three large thought-cloud motifs show purse/coins, a backpack with useful belongings and a group of peers; the heading asks Warum diese Wahl?. A salesperson and a small register appear in the background. No price, utility number or recommended choice is prescribed.
findings.fachlicheCompatibilityWithNewDEENDescrip: Needs/preferences are suggested by practical contents and social context; purse/coins represent budget; visible alternatives and reflection provide a suitable situation for discussing available information. The scene supports the new interaction-of-needs-budget-information text without pretending that a purchase reveals its true cause, that utility is objective/interpersonal, or that one backpack is irrational. It need not illustrate every P-case, a factual default effect or consumer-protection rule; images support orientation, not full assessment.
findings.actual360pxObservation: At actual360×203 the shopper’s reflection, both different backpack alternatives and all three thought motifs are readily identifiable. The single large heading remains readable. The important meaning needs no price tag, small print or background-shop detail.
findings.actual680pxObservation: At actual680×383 the purse/coins, belongings in the practical bag, peers and two products remain clear. The salesperson/register are visibly secondary. Both alternatives fit entirely with no clipping or28rem-cap restriction.
findings.personPerspective: The register screen is turned toward the salesperson, with its back/side toward the main viewer. The thought bubbles are conceptual overlays, not writing in a shopper’s physical notebook. Displayed backpacks have no directional text or instrument markings that would require an actor-facing reading orientation; there is no falsely oriented working document.
findings.styleAndDensity: The same friendly abstract comic language, ivory/navy outlines and teal/orange palette as the development image. Three large thought clouds and two foreground products are economical and legible. No photorealistic redesign, logo, watermark, technical ID, copied worksheet or fake calculation is seen.
findings.altTextAssessment: Existing alt text describes the shopper, two backpacks, budget, practical use and social context correctly. It stays useful under the more explicit discussion text; do not invent an observed motivation, information treatment or image-based performance claim.
findings.recordedMinorLimitationNotBlocker: Available information is represented by the choice situation and reflection, not by a separate explicit information label. An orientation picture is not required to enumerate the complete P-contract, and nothing excludes or misrepresents this factor.
